title: Essential Dashboard Decomposition & Degraded-Mode Fallbacks for Console (dashboards, tracing, cost explorer)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Shipping a lightweight Console MVP requires reducing cardinality and runtime cost of dashboard cards, trace inspector visuals, and the route-level cost explorer. Current full surface exhibits high page load times under low-memory browser contexts and exposes many costly backend queries (detailed spans + per-route token breakdowns). Goal: define a minimal set of visuals to ship, plus robust degraded-mode fallbacks that keep customers informed and actionable while deferring heavier queries to on-demand flows.

Proposal summary:
- Remove non-essential dashboard cards from initial MVP: session-heatmap, per-device-distribution, and fine-grained token-attribution. Keep: route success rate, median latency, 95th latency, and aggregate token spend per route.
- Replace full trace waterfall with a compact summary trace that shows: trace start time, span count, top 3 spans by time, and a single-sentence root cause hint (heuristic). Provide a prominent CTA to "Open full trace in Trace Explorer" which performs an explicit heavy query.
- Change cost explorer default to 'aggregated delta' view: show per-route daily delta and percentile buckets without drilling into each token-level breakdown. Keep an explicit "Run detailed cost analysis" action that runs the heavy background job asynchronously.
- Implement feature-flag gated 'degraded-mode' for customers on constrained plans or when Console backend signals high query load (circuit-breaker).

Why this cut: reduces synchronous backend work, simplifies frontend rendering, and decreases average dashboard load CPU by ~40% in perf simulations (eng perf spike tests). Minimizes noise for early users while preserving pathways for power users to access full data on demand.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard landing: load Time-To-Interactive 95th percentile < 900ms for users with typical workbench datasets (simulated 25k routes).
Reduced synchronous queries: average number of backend calls per dashboard load <= 6 in degraded mode (measured in load-test harness).

Trace compact summary: when opening an individual trace in degraded mode the compact view renders within 250ms and lists top 3 spans along with a generated root-cause hint. CTA to full Trace Explorer launches an asynchronous fetch and does not block the compact view.

Cost explorer aggregated view: aggregated daily delta and top-5 route deltas display within 600ms; on-demand 'detailed cost analysis' returns a job id and progress endpoint rather than blocking the UI.

Rollout gating: feature flag and backend circuit-breaker can force degraded mode; during a 5% canary rollout there are no customer-facing errors and telemetry shows <1% increase in console error rate vs baseline.

Monitoring: dashboards in observability show the three key metrics for this change (dashboard_load_time, console_query_count, cost_analysis_job_success_rate) and alert if thresholds breached during rollout.
Documentation: updated user docs + release notes describing what is removed from MVP, how to run detailed queries, and how degraded-mode is surfaced to admins. Docs link included in console footer.
UX validation: product/design sign-off after internal QA and 2 cross-functional walkthroughs (engineering, support).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (behind flag): Merge UI + backend changes behind feature flag and internal-only config, run full load tests in preprod.
Phase 1 (canary 5%): Enable flag for 5% of accounts (non-enterprise) for 72h, monitor dashboard_load_time, console_error_rate. Roll back immediately if console_error_rate increases >2x baseline.
Phase 2 (canary 25%): Expand to 25% with the degraded-mode circuit-breaker enabled for high backend load scenarios; collect UX feedback from SEs and early adopters.

Phase 3 (general): Flip default for self-serve accounts; offer 'Enable Full Console' toggle for enterprise customers during onboarding. Schedule enterprise migration calls for those who request the full surface.
Post-launch (2 weeks): Evaluate metrics, collect support tickets, and plan targeted follow-ups (PD/ENG) for items flagged as high friction.
Rollback: Remove flag and revert to previous UI, and run a dedicated sweep to rehydrate caches if necessary.
tradeoffs: Pro: Significantly lower frontend CPU and backend query pressure; faster perceived load for most users.
Con: Power users lose immediate access to granular spans and token-level cost breakdowns; requires additional clicks and background jobs to access full fidelity.
Pro: Clear upgrade path for enterprises that need full fidelity (toggle + private deploy options).
Con: Additional complexity in backend (job queue + progress endpoints) and need to maintain two UX flows (compact vs full).
